name: Rosalía
label: Columbia
lede: She won the one flamenco-singing seat at a Barcelona conservatory, then spent a decade refusing to make the same record twice, ending with an orchestral album about saints in 14 languages.

eras.title: A Camarón tape and one seat at the conservatory
eras.text: Rosalía grew up outside Barcelona in a house with no flamenco in it. What she had was a teenage obsession and, by 2014, the one place a year that a Catalan conservatory reserves for flamenco singing.

years.src: Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía · Wikipedia: Rosalía
years.h: Sant Cugat, in a house with no flamenco in it
years.p: Rosalía is born in Sant Cugat del Vallès and raised in Sant Esteve Sesrovires, a Barcelona suburb with no family tradition of Andalusian music.
years.xp: What changed it, in her telling, was a recording of the Cádiz singer [[Camarón de la Isla|1f25c419-4084-40bc-9bac-c39f375384c5]]. Martin Cid Magazine puts her at thirteen when she heard it; Wikipedia says fourteen.

years.h: Kejaleo, then an album called Alaire
years.p: Rosalía sings with the flamenco group Kejaleo from 2012 and is on their 2013 album Alaire, her first record.

years.src: Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía · Wikipedia: Los Ángeles (album)
years.h: One seat a year, and she wins it
years.p: Selected for the flamenco singing course at Barcelona's ESMUC, which takes a single student annually, she studies under José Miguel Vizcaya, known as El Chiqui.
years.xp:
Martin Cid Magazine says Vizcaya's teaching put rigor ahead of enthusiasm, and that the structural knowledge it gave her is what later let her take the form apart on purpose.

She graduated in 2017, with her debut album already recorded.

eras.title: Refree, a guitar and a room in Barcelona
eras.text: Rosalía spends the summer of 2016 in a studio with the guitarist and producer Raül Refree, stripping flamenco to voice, guitar and nerve. Universal signs her, and the Spanish press hears a major talent.

years.h: C. Tangana's 'Antes de morirme' puts her on a dancehall hook
years.p: Sony Music Spain releases [[C. Tangana|46d3689c-23e6-46f7-8ad6-c12f13ac9dea]]'s single, produced by [[Alizzz|a4238edc-daf9-42ed-917b-dd586f91c269]], with Rosalía singing on it. It becomes a sleeper hit two years later.
years.xp: It resurfaces in summer 2018, the same season her own career takes off, and gets a boost from its use in the Netflix series Élite. Wikipedia lists a peak of number 26 on the Spanish chart.

years.h: Recording with Raül Refree at Estudios Calamar
years.p: In Barcelona, [[Raül Refree|0a797765-7506-43ac-8f75-b9e4132b31d6]] serves as co-author, producer, guitarist and arranger on what becomes her debut album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the two met after Refree saw her perform at the Tablao del Carmen. Universal Music signed her in 2016, and the album came out on its Spanish arm.

years.src: Wikipedia: Los Ángeles (album) · Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía
years.h: Los Ángeles: flamenco with the ornament sanded off
years.p: Alegrías, tangos, fandangos and seguidillas, plus covers of Enrique Morente's 'Aunque es de noche' and Bonnie 'Prince' Billy's 'I See a Darkness'.
years.xp:
Specialist audiences found it first. It won the Premio Ruido, the Spanish music press's best national album award, announced January 17, 2018, and ABC and Rockdelux both named it Spain's album of 2017.

AllMusic called it "the appearance of a major talent".

eras.title: Toxic love, one microphone and the whole world listening
eras.text: El Mal Querer turns a 13th-century Occitan novel into eleven chapters of flamenco-pop, and the singles do the rest. By the end of 2019 she has a Latin Grammy for Album of the Year and a reggaeton hit with J Balvin.

years.src: Wikipedia: Malamente · Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía
years.h: 'Malamente' opens the book
years.p: The lead single is Chapter 1 of El Mal Querer, released May 30, 2018 on Columbia with a video from the Barcelona production company Canada.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it was recorded in 2017 at Casa Arte on El Hierro in the Canary Islands. Pitchfork later named it the 23rd best song of the 2010s.

Not everyone in flamenco was sold. Martin Cid Magazine quotes the veteran singer José Mercé saying not everything is valid, and that any small thing is not flamenco.

years.h: Made in El Guincho's Barcelona apartment with one microphone
years.p: Rosalía says she was in the red when the album came out; she and [[El Guincho|7e57d8a2-e6eb-48dd-8e50-ff7eaa412ccb]] recorded it with a computer, a microphone and an audio interface.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the setup and says Rosalía put her own money into what she treated as a university project, with the concept developed alongside her friend Ferran Echegaray.

years.src: Wikipedia: El Mal Querer · Wikipedia: Rosalía
years.h: El Mal Querer: eleven chapters, one bad relationship
years.p: Each track is a chapter of the anonymous novel Flamenca, produced by El Guincho and Rosalía. Pitchfork named it the sixth best album of 2018.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 89. Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne wrote that hers was "as commanding a presence as Spanish-language pop has encountered in ages". Alexis Petridis gave it five stars in The Guardian.

Singles followed in a chain: 'Pienso en tu mirá' in July, 'Di mi nombre' three days before the album, 'Bagdad' in December and 'De aquí no sales' in January 2019.

years.h: 'Con Altura' makes her a pop star
years.p: With [[J Balvin|5bdeb32d-56a5-4b6d-a768-264101fa0a0a]] and El Guincho, the single arrives with a Director X video that becomes the most-watched female music video on YouTube in 2019.
years.xp:
It began in September 2018 in Miami, and its title comes from a phrase by the Dominican influencer Mariachi Budda that the track samples. Wikipedia reports over 1.5 billion streams in 2019.

The video won two MTV VMAs, Best Latin and Best Choreography, making her the first Spanish artist to win at the ceremony. Balvin had put her on his 2018 song 'Brillo' first.

years.cap: 28 De Abril De 2023. DISFRUTAN 160 MIL ASISTENTES CONCIERTO DE ROSALÍA EN EL ZÓCALO CAPITALINO CON SU MOTOMAMI WORLD... · Wikimedia
years.src: Rolling Stone: Latin Grammys 2019 · GRAMMY.com: Bad Bunny, Rosalía
yt: Album of the Year acceptance, 2019 Latin Grammys
years.h: Latin Grammys: Album of the Year for El Mal Querer
years.p: At 26 she becomes the second solo woman to win the night's top prize, after Shakira in 2006, and thanks J Balvin from the stage.
years.xp:
Grammy.com quotes her on winning: "I'm serious, I'm in shock. This is the last thing I expected." She also took Best Urban Song for 'Con Altura' and performed a medley that night.

Sources differ on the total: Wikipedia counts six wins for the album, while Grammy.com's recap lists five awards for her.

eras.title: Everybody's favorite guest verse
eras.text: Between tours she becomes the most in-demand guest in pop: Travis Scott, Bad Bunny, Arca, Billie Eilish. In the middle of it, in Miami during the pandemic, the next album starts to take shape.

years.h: First Spanish woman to perform at the Grammys
years.p: At the 62nd Grammys she plays the show and is nominated for Best New Artist, a first for a Spanish-speaking act; El Mal Querer wins Best Latin Rock, Urban or Alternative Album.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists her as the first Spanish woman to perform at the Grammys, and the first Spanish-speaking act nominated for Best New Artist.

years.h: 'TKN' with Travis Scott lands on the Hot 100
years.p: The May 2020 single with [[Travis Scott|e4a51f17-a57b-47b1-b37b-f552d0f8e9e6]] debuts at number 66 on the Billboard Hot 100 and goes viral on TikTok; its video wins a Latin Grammy for Best Short Form Music Video.
years.xp: A month later, on June 22, came 'KLK', her collaboration with the producer [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], on his album KiCk i.

years.h: Bad Bunny's 'La Noche de Anoche' drops on Valentine's Day
years.p: The single from [[Bad Bunny|89aa5ecb-59ad-46f5-b3eb-2d424e941f19]]'s El Último Tour del Mundo, with Rosalía, debuts at number two on Spotify's global chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports 6.63 million first-day streams, the biggest debut for a Spanish-language song on Spotify at that point.

years.h: 'La Fama' with The Weeknd: an experimental bachata
years.p: The lead single from Motomami, with [[The Weeknd|c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9]], becomes her seventh number one in Spain.
years.xp: A month later, in December 2021, Rockstar Games launched a Grand Theft Auto Online radio station called Motomami Los Santos, curated by Rosalía and Arca.

eras.title: Motomami: pistons, filters and chaos
eras.text: She trades the flamenco storyline for experimental reggaeton: hard drums, vocal chops, ballads that curdle. Critics rate it the best-reviewed record of 2022, and a runway stage show follows.

years.h: 'Saoko' shoots its video in Kyiv
years.p: The second Motomami single is filmed at Podilskyi Bridge; the video later wins the MTV VMA for Best Editing.

years.h: Motomami: Pitchfork gives it 8.4 and Best New Music
years.p: Columbia releases it March 18, 2022; Metacritic calls it the best-reviewed album of the year.
years.xp:
The title honors her mother Pilar Tobella, who used to get her around town on a motorcycle; her mother's company, Motomami S.L., was set up in 2018. Rosalía has described the record as split between a strong, experimental Moto side and a personal, confessional Mami side.

It was recorded between March 2020 and August 2021 in Barcelona, New York (including Electric Lady), Los Angeles and Miami, with producers including [[Noah Goldstein|2dad5809-0d9b-40cf-85cf-2f8828ffaaf0]], [[Pharrell Williams|149f91ef-1287-46da-9a8e-87fee02f1471]], [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]], Frank Dukes and El Guincho.

years.cap: Rosalía at Chile, Motomami tour. 28/08/2022-Movistar Arena · Wikimedia
years.h: Motomami World Tour opens in Almería
years.p: A white cyclorama, two vertical screens and a 20-meter runway; the crew grows from about 40 to over 150. It ends December 18 in Paris.
years.xp: Tour manager Agustín Boffi said the crew expanded to "over 150 people" from 40 on the previous cycle. Dates included Madrid's WiZink Center, London's O2, Radio City Music Hall and Mexico City's Auditorio Nacional; the São Paulo show was moved to a bigger venue.

years.h: 'Despechá' arrives three weeks into the tour
years.p: The song on the Motomami deluxe edition becomes a global hit.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as a track that began life in the live show before it was released.

years.h: Second Latin Grammy for Album of the Year
years.p: Motomami takes Album of the Year, making Rosalía the first woman to win it twice as lead artist. It also won at the Grammys in February 2023 for Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rolling Stone, Pitchfork, The New York Times and W Magazine criticized the Recording Academy for leaving the album out of the main Grammy Album of the Year race.

years.h: RR: an EP with Rauw Alejandro
years.p: The joint EP with [[Rauw Alejandro|197b70c7-8910-4030-ad03-632d82aa40e3]] carries the single 'Beso', which becomes a global success.

years.h: 'Oral': a charity single with Björk
years.p: Björk wrote it in 1998 and shelved it as too poppy; she revived it in 2023 with Rosalía and both gave the income to AEGIS, a group fighting salmon farming in Iceland.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the proceeds go to legal fees for Icelandic activists opposing open net-pen fish farming. The video, directed by Carlota Guerrero, uses AI-generated deepfake versions of both singers.

eras.title: Lux: strings, saints and a Berghain
eras.text: Three years of work, the London Symphony Orchestra, lyrics in 14 languages and one female saint behind each song. The reviews are the best of her career, and the arena tour that follows plays like an opera-ballet.

q: Why do you have to destroy the song always?
years.src: AOL: How a Fight with Her Sister · HIGHXTAR: Rosalía talks to Apple Music
years.h: Her sister asks why she always destroys the song
years.p: Pili, Rosalía's sister, stylist and creative director, said it in a car while listening to Motomami. Rosalía has said it stung, and changed how she wrote.
years.xp:
Ahead of Lux, Rosalía said the remark made her ask whether she was finishing her thoughts: "Maybe I'm writing songs, but I'm not finishing the thought." The result, she said, let her grow as writer, arranger and producer.

She told Apple Music: "MOTOMAMI was minimalist; this is maximalism. Brutalism."

years.h: 'Berghain' with Björk and Yves Tumor opens the Lux era
years.p: Sung in German, Spanish and English, it debuts at number one in Spain. The video, shot in Warsaw, is directed by Nicolás Méndez of the production company Canada.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rosalía wrote it with Björk, Yves Tumor and the producers Noah Goldstein, Sir Dylan and Jake Miller. It reached number 22 on the Billboard Global 200, and The Guardian named it one of the 20 best songs of 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lux (Rosalía album) · Soap Central: Pitchfork rates Rosalía's Lux · Fridge Cigarette: A Vibes-Based Review · NPR: On 'Lux,' Rosalía
yt: The Zane Lowe Interview on Lux
years.h: Lux: Pitchfork gives it 8.6 and Best New Music
years.p: Columbia releases it with the London Symphony Orchestra. Pitchfork later ranks it No. 16 on its 50 best albums of 2025.
years.xp:
Lux is in four movements, with songs inspired by saints including Hildegard of Bingen, Joan of Arc, Teresa of Ávila and Saint Rosalia of Palermo, and lyrics in 14 languages per Wikipedia (NPR and Apple Music say 13). Daníel Bjarnason conducts the LSO; guests include Björk, Carminho, Estrella Morente, Sílvia Pérez Cruz and Yahritza y su Esencia, and among the producers are Caroline Shaw and Pharrell Williams. It was announced October 20, 2025.

Pitchfork called it "a heartfelt offering of avant-garde classical pop that roars through genre, romance, and religion." Metacritic scores it 95, The Guardian and Rolling Stone gave five stars, and The Guardian and Consequence made it their number one of 2025. Wikipedia reports 42.1 million Spotify streams on day one, a record for a female Spanish-language artist.

years.h: 'La Perla' with Yahritza y su Esencia tops the Spanish chart
years.p: Rosalía performs it solo on The Tonight Show, staged after The Princess and the Pea; it becomes the album's second single on December 5.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists number one in Spain and Argentina, number three on Hot Latin Songs and number 12 on the Global 200. It is her 13th number one in Spain. The video, directed by Stillz (Matías Vásquez), who also worked on Motomami visuals, came out December 16.

years.h: Brit Awards: 'Berghain' with Björk, and a first for Spanish
years.p: Rosalía performs the song with Björk and becomes the first Spanish-speaking winner of International Artist of the Year.
years.xp: The performance was accompanied by the Heritage Orchestra. In May 2026 she also won International Songwriter of the Year at the Ivor Novello Awards.

years.cap: Rosalía opening her show at Unipol Forum in Milan · Wikimedia
years.h: Lux Tour opens outside Lyon with an orchestra on a cross-shaped stage
years.p: Fifty-seven shows through September 16, including London's O2 (May 5-6) and Madison Square Garden (June 16-17).
years.xp:
The show runs in four acts and an intermezzo, from ballet and religious imagery to a darker electronic persona, with the Heritage Orchestra, conducted by Yudania Gómez Heredia, on a B-stage laid out as a Latin cross.

Alexis Petridis called it "one of the boldest, most highbrow arena shows in pop history"; Rolling Stone called it "part opera, part ballet, part pop extravaganza".

years.h: A guest spot on Fontaines D.C.'s Dopamine Chamber
years.p: Wikipedia lists her on the track 'Where Is Gone?' from [[Fontaines D.C.|fd87acc7-e0a0-4a45-bc2a-d2ab5c10be68]]'s album Dopamine Chamber, dated September 17, 2026.
